queries: Direct lookup: TruthfulQA (arXiv 2109.07958) on why false answers arise
Direct lookup: InstructGPT paper (arXiv 2203.02155) on hallucination reduction without grounding

sources_considered.why: Attributes false answers to imitating the training distribution; partial fit with the causal story.
Shows text-only fine-tuning reduced but did not remove hallucination; bears on 'no capacity to avoid'.

receipt.public_excerpt: However, this result is expected if false answers are learned from the training distribution.

evidence_items.explanation: Links falsehoods to imitating training text, which partly fits Marcus's word-statistics story. It does not test whether grounding in the world is the missing factor.

receipt.public_excerpt:
InstructGPT models make up information not present in the input about half as often as GPT-3 (a
21% vs. 41% hallucination rate, respectively).

evidence_items.explanation: Human-feedback fine-tuning, with no grounding in the world, halved fabrication but left it at 21%. This fits 'cannot reliably avoid' and also shows some capacity to reduce errors, so the causal story stays unsettled.

unresolved_gaps: No controlled study available isolates text-only training, as against world grounding, as the cause of misinformation in GPT-3.
Whether 'no capacity to avoid' means 'never' or 'not reliably' changes how e2 bears on the claim.
